{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]]

'''Indian ice-cream''' or '''''sxusem''''' (pronounced "s-khushem", with "kh" sound resembling the final sound in the Scottish word 'loch') is a [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]] made by native people throughout the Pacific Northwest region of North America. Traditionally this foam was eaten at larger gatherings with wooden spoons and children were known to play with the foam, sometimes throwing it at each other. Indian ice-cream contains saponins, and it is refreshing but a little bitter.

==Ingredients==
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] [[Cookbook:Buffaloberry|soapberries (Canada buffaloberries)]]
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] water
*optional sweeteners may include fireweed, camas bulb (Camassia quamash) or sweet berries such as salal berries (Gaultheria shallon), or thimbleberries. Nowadays many people sweeten it with [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]].

==Procedure==
#Crush berries to release the liquid/juice.
#Combine juice with an equal part of water.
#Add sweetener.
#Whip it with a [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] until foamy, similar in texture to [[Cookbook:Whipped cream|whipped cream]]. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* A branch of soapberries can be shaken over a metal or glass container until all of the ripe berries fall off. Oily or plastic containers will prevent frothing.
